top_signal.title: My mom is worried about her struggling footwear business, and I want to help her save it. Where should we start?
top_signal.summary: Hi everyone! I'm posting because my mom has been worrying about her business, and I genuinely want to help her figure out how to turn things around. It’s difficult seeing her struggle when she has put so much effort into this business, and I want to do whatever I can to help her succeed. I’m hoping to learn from people who have experience running businesses, marketing products, or navigating similar challenges. I would really appreciate honest feedback, even if it means hearing things we might need to change.   We run a small Filipino footwear brand that sells ballet flats primarily through Shopee, Lazada, and TikTok Shop. Our products are made in Marikina City, the Philippines’ Shoe Capital, where shoemaking has a long-standing tradition. Our ballet flats are priced at around  ₱520 per pair (approximately US$9, not $27.84) .   We want to offer customers more than just another pair of shoes. Our products represent the craftsmanship of Marikina shoemakers and the work of Filipino artisans.  One reason behind our pricing is our commitment to paying our employees at least the applicable minimum wage.  We believe the people who make our products deserve fair compensation for their labor and skills. While some footwear manufacturers may keep costs lower through different labor practices, we don’t want our business to depend on paying workers below the legal minimum.
